1.why: Every MFA record is keyed solely by session.accountId and no endpoint accepts a user-supplied identifier, so only the authenticated owner can view or modify their own MFA settings.

2.why: Identity codes are bound to a per-signin preToken and its specific accountId, and TOTP secrets are per-account, so a code issued for one user cannot authenticate any other user.

3.why: /api/mfa/confirm sets record.active = true but never deletes or rotates other entries in the sessions map, so any prior sessions for that account continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encryptSecret) and recovery codes are stored only as peppered HMAC-SHA-256 hashes (recoveryHash).

5.why: All tokens, six-digit codes, TOTP secrets, recovery codes, IVs, the pepper, and the AES key are produced by crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: The client uses no localStorage/sessionStorage, keeps the CSRF token and provisioning secret only in JS memory/DOM, and both cookies (__Host-session, __Host-preauth) are HttpOnly.

7.why: Email, phone, OTP, and recovery code inputs are all validated server-side with strict allow-list regexes (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, normaliseRecovery) plus typed JSON body checks.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (the only innerHTML assignments use static strings), and a per-response nonce CSP without unsafe-inline blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The application issues no HTTP redirects at all and navigation is confined to internal SPA view switches, so no open redirect is possible, though no explicit allow-list mechanism exists to inspect.

10.why: securityHeaders sets CSP (nonce-based, frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: secureCookie applies HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict to both the session and pre-auth cookies.

12.why: In the default TEST_MODE (NODE_ENV !== 'production') the mock identity code and newly issued recovery codes are deliberately written to the browser console and the on-page Logs panel, even though seeds, session tokens, URLs, and error output are kept clean and stack traces are suppressed.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes and are marked used then deleted, TOTP codes are confined to a 30-second window with usedSetupCounters replay protection, and recovery codes are single-use.

14.why: Both identity verification and the MFA endpoints track failedAttempts and impose a 10-minute lockout (429) after 5 consecutive failures.

15.why: A fresh randomToken session identifier is issued upon authentication while the pre-auth cookie is expired, idle (15 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced, and logout deletes the session server-side.
